title: In Hieremiam Prophetam Libri Sex
author: Jerome

passages.original: simul sapientes et fatui sunt; doctrina eorum pro qualitate ingenii uel uilis est et ligno conparatur uel similis argento propter eloquii uenustatem; affertur de Tharsis — uel Indiae regio est, ut uult Iosephus, uel certe omne pelagus Tharsis appellatur et caeli habet similitudinem — et tamen inuoluta est uerborum artificio; si enim patuerit, decipere non poterit. et aurum de Ophaz.
passages.english: They are at once wise and foolish; their teaching, according to the quality of their talent, is either cheap and compared to wood, or like silver because of the charm of its eloquence; it is brought from Tarshish (either it is a region of India, as Josephus holds, or certainly the whole sea is called Tarshish and bears a likeness to the sky) and yet it is wrapped up in the artifice of words; for if it were laid open, it could not deceive. And gold from Ophaz.

passages.original: unde et Iosephus refert de sacerdotali genere ac tribu Leui fuisse principes, quibus successerit Herodes. Antipatri proselyti filius, et postea sub Uespasiano regnum huius generis, immo imaginem imperii. penitus fuisse deletam.
passages.english: Hence Josephus too reports that there had been rulers from the priestly family and the tribe of Levi, whom Herod, the son of Antipater the proselyte, succeeded, and that afterwards, under Vespasian, the kingdom of this race, or rather the semblance of rule, was utterly destroyed.
passages.notes: The punctuation of the edition (full stops after 'Herodes' and 'imperii') breaks the sentence. It is read here as one continuous sentence in indirect speech dependent on 'refert'.
